Kaneki desktop app: build plan

What gets built, in which order, who owns which piece, and the decisions behind it: eight part plans written by sub-agents, reviewed against the code and merged into one.

The plan in one screen

In short

Build the app in eight parts across milestones M0–M5, about 69 working days for one person, of which about 37 reach M2, the point where gates are decided in the app instead of in Zed panes. The Python harness computes everything; the native Host only carries data; the UI only renders. Three tracks can start today with nothing to install. The Host stack is decided: Go + Wails only (owner, 2026-11-18). All twelve recommended decisions were accepted on 2026-11-18. S1S2

8part plans (P1–P8)
~37 dto M2: watch every ticket, decide gates
~69 dto M5: sessions, cost, installer
12 / 13decisions accepted (macOS open)
~29×real tokens vs the harness count
  1. Logic lives in the harness. Four new read-only sdlc commands (contract, ticket-detail, gate-request, cost) replace the logic three parts wanted to copy into the Go Host. S3
  2. Start now, no installs: the harness commands (P1), the UI against fixture files in Edge (P4) and the cost engine (P7). P2 (Go + Wails setup and spike) waits for your install approval. S2
  3. The mock's "reject and reopen" does nothing. gate --status rejected only sets the verdict and drops --reopen; the real runs needed a second invalidate command. Decision: make it one atomic harness command. S4S5
  4. A spawned session could ship by itself. The git guard checks shell git only, not sdlc ship; the app adds its own deny layer. S6S7
  5. Real cost is about 29× the harness count on both test tickets, measured from the Claude Code session logs. S8S9
  6. macOS is possible with Wails, but the plan is Windows-first in about ten places; recommended as a later milestone M6. OPEN

How the app is built: UI, Host, harness

Three layers, each with one job. The UI draws what it is given. The Host (a small Go program built with Wails) runs commands, watches files and starts Claude sessions. The harness, the Python CLI that already exists, is the only thing that computes ticket state and the only thing that writes ticket files. S10

The rule in one sentenceIf a value needs ticket rules to compute (who it is waiting on, which nodes go stale, whether a gate may close), the harness computes it; the Host and UI only pass it on.

That rule settled most conflicts between the part plans. P5 wanted the Host to work out "waiting on user" and the stale preview, P3 refreshed through status-of --path, P7 debated a native log parser. All three now call a harness command instead. S3

Harness changes the app depends on (all in kaneki-harness)

Command or changeGives the appKindPart
sdlc contractcontractVersion, harness version, command list; checked at start-upreadP1
sdlc tickets (extended)title, waitingOn / waitingNode / waitingReason, per-node generation and boundaryreadP1
sdlc ticket-detailnode cards, unit records, loop-backs, tracereadP1
sdlc gate-requesteverything the gate dialog shows: readiness dry run, evidence, choices with exact argv and stale previewreadP1
sdlc costreal tokens and cost from session logs, per ticket / node / model / dayreadP7
N4 fixstatus --accept-current-state takes the ticket lockwrite fixP1
Atomic reject (new H10)gate --status rejected --reopen X also invalidates Xwrite changeP1

Each harness call costs about half a second of Python start-up. The Host hides it with a cache: one call per changed ticket when a file changes, none when the UI re-renders. S11

What gets built when

Data contract first, then the UI and the Host in parallel, then one milestone per feature. The UI can be built against fixture files before the Host exists, so the stack choice does not hold it up.

  1. Now, no installs P1 · P4 · P7

    Harness commands with tests, schemas and fixtures; UI shell running on fixtures in Edge (?source=fixture); cost.py; and you run the one hook-capture session (P6-S0a).

  2. Wails setup P2

    Install Go + Wails on D:\toolchains, build the small spike slice, measure it, record D10 (closed: Go/Wails), scaffold the app.

  3. M1 · read-only app P3 + P4

    Host core wired to the UI. Done when parity.mjs shows zero differences from sdlc web for both real tickets.

  4. M2 · gates in the app P5

    Gate dialog, command preview and confirm, invalidate, lane, toasts. Proven on a throwaway ticket, never on the real ones.

  5. M3 · M4 · M5 P6 · P7 · P8

    Sessions run node by node under a policy; the cost tab; first run, new ticket, worktree cleanup, installer, CI.

Effort: the sum of each part's task ceilings (S ≤ 2 h, M ≤ 1 day, L ≤ 3 days) S2

ScopeCeilingRealistic (~60 %)
M0–M2 (P1–P5): watch every ticket, decide gates~61 days~37 days
M3–M5 (P6–P8): sessions, cost, setup, installer~54 days~32 days
Total (117 tasks: 43 S · 59 M · 15 L)~115 days~69 days

The 60 % factor is a planning judgement, not a measurement: the ceilings count some shared work twice (fixtures, discovery, process handling), which the review merged. INFERRED

What the app may run

The Host refuses any command not on this list before starting a process, and never builds a shell string. S11

Host allowlist, v1

ClassCommands
readcontract, tickets, ticket-detail, gate-request, status, plan, validate, digest, status-of, cost, lang (no --set), receipts (no --reissue)
write, M2gate (always --actor user), invalidate (reason required), lane --set full
write, M5init (never --force), onboard-scan, onboard-verify (no tests), onboard-write (first run only)
nevership, ship-request, review-fetch, git, install, zed-setup, web, record, handback, receipts --reissue, status --accept-current-state
git (separate list)worktree list --porcelain, worktree remove <path> (no --force), status --porcelain, rev-parse, log; no branch, push, commit, reset, clean, prune

Note: install, onboard-write, zed-setup and web sit in the harness's READ_ONLY set (so they take no ticket lock) even though they write files or open a port. That is why they are listed explicitly rather than allowed by class. S17

Real cost against the harness count

The harness counts only what agents report about themselves. The session logs also contain the driver session, retries and every cache re-read, so the real number is about 29 times larger on both tickets. The design plan's "~1.4M vs ~20M+" figure was an early snapshot and is out of date. S8S9S10

Can it be installed on a Mac?

Answer

Yes, it can be, but not as the plan stands today. Wails builds macOS apps, and the harness, Claude Code and Zed all run on a Mac. The plan is Windows-first in about ten places, and a Mac build has to be made and signed on a Mac. Recommended: ship Windows first, keep the code portable from the start, add the Mac build as milestone M6. INFERRED

Why inferred: the framework facts (Wails targets macOS, uses the system WebKit view there, and needs a Mac to build a Mac app) come from knowledge of the frameworks, not from re-reading their current docs. Task P2-T01 checks them before the spike slice. The Windows-specific items below are verified in the part plans. S12S7S15

Do now (cheap)

Everything OS-specific behind P3's platform module; folders from the stack's path API, never hard-coded; build scripts in Node, not PowerShell; UI tested in a WebKit browser once.

Do at M6

Mac PTY and process groups, .dmg packaging, the macOS CI job, notifications, Telex check on the Mac, and the signing decision if the app goes beyond your own machine.
Effect on the stack choiceNone: D10 is decided (Go + Wails). Notifications, single instance and the updater come from Go libraries on both platforms; P2-T01 checks them. INFERRED
Question for youDo you have a Mac to test on? Without one, M6 can still produce an unsigned build from a macos-latest CI runner, but nobody can check Telex input or the terminal on real hardware.

Risks to watch

Top risks across the build S2

RiskSeverityMitigation
Session supervision does not behave as hoped (hooks, permission prompts, questions inside a terminal the app owns)HighSpikes S0a–S0c before any M3 code; M0–M2 stand on their own
A spawned session ships, commits, pushes or deletes a branchHighPolicy locked in code, --disallowedTools, an app-injected deny hook, the Host never runs those commands, a post-node git log check, tests for every deny case
Harness changes break CLI users or sdlc webMediumAdditive keys only, contractVersion, the existing 72 tests plus new ones, one assertion update
Real data has no pending gate to test againstMediumFixtures generated by the harness itself; one throwaway ticket for M2
Disk space on D: (14.4 GB free)LowGo + Wails is about 0.5 GB under D: oolchains; check free space before the install
Claude Code changes its log format and breaks costLowDefensive parsing, a cache schema version, a canary check at start-up
